comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe the launch of new processor families in 2024 to address data center and AI workloads. Intel specifically launched the Intel Xeon 6 processors, differentiating them by Efficient-cores (E-Cores) for scale-out workloads and Performance-cores (P-Cores) with matrix engines for compute-intensive tasks like AI. AMD reports that its Data Center segment revenue growth was primarily driven by higher sales of its AMD EPYC CPUs, which is Intel's direct competitor to the Xeon family. While Intel details the architectural shift to a hybrid core design for its new launch, AMD quantifies the market success of its existing EPYC CPU line through significant revenue increases.

sentences.text: In 2024, we launched the Intel Xeon 6 processors with Efficient-cores (or E-Cores) and Performance-cores (or P-cores).

Our E-core processors feature single-threaded cores for scale-out, parallel workloads, while our P-core processors feature hyperthreaded cores and built-in matrix engines that are designed for more compute-intensive workloads such as AI.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI Inference Platforms and Cloud Services
comparisons.peer_summary: The company launched AI inference platforms combining software with Ada, Hopper, and Grace Hopper processors for generative AI and LLMs. It also introduced NVIDIA DGX Cloud and AI Foundations to help businesses create and operate custom large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight the launch of new products in 2024 tailored for AI and data center workloads. Intel launched Intel Xeon 6 processors featuring built-in matrix engines designed for compute-intensive workloads such as AI. NVIDIA launched AI inference platforms that combine full-stack inference software with processors (Ada, Hopper, Grace Hopper) optimized for generative AI, LLMs, and other AI workloads. Both disclosures center on the strategic introduction of hardware capable of handling the growing demand for AI processing in the data center.

sentences.text: Our E-core processors feature single-threaded cores for scale-out, parallel workloads, while our P-core processors feature hyperthreaded cores and built-in matrix engines that are designed for more compute-intensive workloads such as AI.
